MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  October 13, 2020
Due to COVID-19 and the “Stay at Home” Order for the State of California and the Social
Distance Guidelines issued by Federal, State, and Local Authorities this Council Meeting was
conducted via Video Teleconferencing for all Council and Staff with the exception of the City
Attorney and City Clerk who were present in the Council Chamber. All public comments that
were emailed to the City Clerk were read during the meeting.

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Goodell
at 5:00 p.m., on October 13, 2020, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on October 8 , 2020, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Teleconferenced:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Goodell

Absent:  None

Staff  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Teleconferenced:  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services

Staff Present:  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Acting Assistant City Clerk

RECESS AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Goodell recessed the meeting. The City Council reconvened at
6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

INVOCATION: Council Member Bucknum

City Council Minutes  1  October 13, 2020
 PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Raths

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Recognize Gayle Wood for Being Named "Volunteer of the Year" by Camp Pendleton

  Mayor Goodell virtually presented a proclamation to Gayle Wood.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The following public comments were received and read by the City Clerk.

Gail Reavis, M.V.: Expressed concern about complaints from the last meeting regarding the
placement of Candidate Schlicht’s campaign signs and requested that the City Council Meetings be
open to the public in the council chamber.

Daniel Avery, M.V.: Complained about Candidate Raths’ campaign signs that are in violation of
the City’s Sign Policy.

Catherine Palmer, M.V.: Requested that the City implement Community Choice Energy.

The Following spoke against Proposition 16 and encouraged voters to vote no: Teame Ozaqbe; Sue
Zhao; Ashley Owen, M.V.; Alan Song; and Bethany Hernandez.

Robert Fecher, M.V.: Asked the Council to consider a moratorium on garage sales within the City
to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-19.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Criticized the City Council and City Attorney for extending Council Member
terms.

CONSENT CALENDAR

For the record the City Clerk announced there was a duplicate resolution in the agenda packet for
item 24, but the recommended action is correct on the agenda.

Items 12 and 23 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  2  October 13, 2020
 1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of September 8, 2020, as
  presented.

2.  Check Register Dated August 28, 2020 in the Amount of $1,073,389.64

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated September 4, 2020 in the Amount of $2,623,349.09

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated September 11, 2020 in the Amount of $1,185,256.25

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register Dated September 23, 2020 in the Amount of $722,743.26

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Check Register Dated September 25, 2020 in the Amount of $1,065,487.91

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

7.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August 2020

  Received and filed.

8.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for August 2020

  Received and filed.

9.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report
  for August 2020

  Received and filed.

10. Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for August 2020

  Received and filed.

11. Quarterly Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo - Fiscal Year End June 30, 2020

  Received and filed.

13. City of Mission Viejo Conflict of Interest Code

City Council Minutes  3  October 13, 2020
   Adopted Resolution 20-42 Amending the City of Mission Viejo Conflict of Interest Code.

14. Recreation Management Software Contract Extension

  (1) Approved contract extension agreement and issuance of purchase orders to PerfectMind
  Inc. for recreation management platform and support for 2-year term in an amount not to
  exceed $64,600 and (2) authorized staff to extend contract term with PerfectMind Inc. for up
  to 3 additional years in an amount not to exceed $108,000 for a total 5-year amount not to
  exceed $172,600.

15. Orange County Transportation Authority 2020-2021 Comprehensive Transportation
  Funding Program Call-for-Projects

  (1) Adopted Resolution 20-43 Approving the Submittal of the Santa Margarita Parkway and
  Crown Valley Parkway Corridor Improvement Projects to the Orange County Transportation
  Authority (OCTA) for Funding Under the Competitive Measure M2 Regional Transportation
  Signal Synchronization Program (Project P); and (2) directed staff to transmit Resolution 20-
  43 to OCTA by October 22, 2020, in conjunction with the City's funding application for said
  projects.

16. Highway Safety Improvement Program (HSIP) Call for Projects - Cycle 10 - Citywide
  Installation of Audible Pedestrian Push Button Systems at Signalized Intersections

  (1) Adopted Resolution 20-44 Authorizing the Director of Public Works to Submit an
  Application for Highway Safety Improvement Program (HSIP) Grant Funds for the Prioritized
  Installation of Audible Pedestrian Push Button Systems at Signalized Intersections; and (2)
  directed staff to transmit said Resolution to Caltrans by October 19, 2020, in conjunction with
  the City's funding application for said project.

17. Christopher Park Play Area Renovations (CIP 312) - Notice of Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City Clerk
  to record Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the Faithful
  Performance and Payment Bonds one year and thirty- five (35) days respectively, after the
  date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed
  with the City and (4) authorized the payment of the final retention of $22,364.13, thirty-five
  (35) days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.

18. Craycraft Park Restroom Construction (CIP 315) - Notice of Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City Clerk
  to record Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the Faithful
  Performance and Payment Bonds one year and thirty- five (35) days respectively, after the
  date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed
  with the City and (4) authorized the payment of the final retention of $8,781.63, thirty-five
  (35) days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.

City Council Minutes  4  October 13, 2020
 19. Mission Viejo Aquatics Complex - Dive Dry Training Area Shade Cover Replacement

  (1) Awarded Contract to Southern Hemisphere Shade, Inc.(A20-29) for the replacement of
  storm damaged shade cloth for an amount not to exceed $58,480.00; and (2) issued a purchase
  order for an amount not to exceed $58.480.00.

20. Purchase of Motorola Dispatch and Radio Communications Equipment for Animal
  Services

  Approved the purchase of dispatch and radio communications equipment from Motorola
  Solutions at a cost of $37,245.09.

21. Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center Flooring Rehabilitation

  Approved second amendment for Shaw Industries, Inc. DBA Shaw Integrated Solutions for
  purchase and installation of extra flooring and transition materials for the floor the remaining
  meeting rooms and staff areas at Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center for period
  of June 23, 2020 to June 30, 2021 in an amount not to exceed $235,375.04.

22. Issuance of Revenue Bonds by the California Municipal Finance Authority (CMFA) in
  an Aggregate Principal Amount Not to Exceed $3,500,000 to Finance and Refinance
  Certain Facilities for Vocational Visions and Certain Other Matters Relating Thereto .

  Adopted Resolution 20-45 Approving the Issuance of the Bonds by the CMFA for the benefit
  of Vocational Visions, a nonprofit public benefit corporation as described in section 501(c)(3)
  of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 (the "Borrower") to provide for the financing of the
  Project, such adoption is solely for the purposes of satisfying the requirements of TEFRA, the
  Code and the California Government Code Section 6500 (and following).

24. Designation of Positions as Authorized Agents to Apply for Federal and State Financial
  Assistance

  (1) Adopted Resolution 20-46 Authorizing Certain Positions to Act as Agents for the Purpose
  of Obtaining Federal Financial Assistance and/or State Financial Assistance for Federal Fiscal
  Year 2019 as part of the Emergency Management Performance Grant Program; (2) adopted
  Resolutions 20-47 Authorizing Certain Positions to Act as Agents for the Purpose of
  Obtaining Federal Financial Assistance and/or State Financial Assistance for Federal Fiscal
  Year 2020 as part of the Emergency Management Performance Grant Program; and (3)
  adopted Resolution 20-48 a Universal Resolution Authorizing Certain Positions to Act as
  Agents for the Purpose of Obtaining Federal Financial Assistance and/or State Financial
  Assistance for a period of three years.

25. Modifications to the City of Mission Viejo Purchasing and Policy Procedure Manual for
  Cal-Card Purchases during emergency and/or disaster response

  (1) Adopted Resolution 20-49 Adopting the Purchasing Policy and Procedures Manual with
  revisions related to Emergency Cal-Card Purchases; and (2) approved travel-related Cal-Card
  purchases for the recent deployment of Animal Services personnel to the Butte County fires
  in the amount of $3,422.88.
City Council Minutes  5  October 13, 2020
 ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

12. Year End Financial Report for the Golf Course Fund

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Council Member Sachs commended staff for how well they have financially managed the golf
  course during the pandemic.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to receive and
  file the report.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

23. Jeronimo Road & Marguerite Parkway Intersection Improvements (CIP 21246)

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley gave kudos to Assistant City Engineer Joe Ames and Director of
  Public Works Mark Chagnon for their efforts in obtaining grants for this project.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, authorize
  issuance of a purchase order to civTEC in an amount not to exceed $63,750 for design
  engineering services for the subject project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

26. Fiscal Year 2019/20 Close Out Report and Fiscal Year 2020/21 Budget Adjustments for
  Certain Revenue and Expenditure Accounts

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley to create a CIP and designate $75,000 for the design
  of Coronado Park from park development fees. The motion failed for lack of a second.

  Council Member Bucknum and Council Member Sachs asked Mayor Pro Tem Kelley to bring
  a separate report at the next City Council Meeting for discussion.

  Mayor Goodell suggested a staff report to discuss the renovation schedule of the parks.

City Council Minutes  6  October 13, 2020
   Council Member Sachs asked that the City Council discuss the Comprehensive Annual Leave
  Buy-Back Program at a later date.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to (1)
  Adopt Resolution 20-50 Amending the FY 2019/20 City Budget for Year-End Close Out
  Adjustments in Certain Accounts and Funds; (2) adopt Resolution 20-51 Amending the FY
  2020/21 City Budget.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

27. Oso Creek Golf Course - Turfgrass Maintenance Equipment Lease Purchase

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to (1) adopt
  Resolution 20-52 Authorizing Execution and Delivery of an Equipment Lease-Purchase
  Agreement and Approving Related Documents and Actions; and (2) approve the 60-month
  Lease Agreement with U.S. Bancorp Government Leasing and Finance, Inc.(A20-30) and
  Authorized Staff to Execute Agreement with a Principal Amount Not to Exceed $143,000;
  (3) authorize City staff to sign the sales proposal with Turf Star, Inc. to initiate the order; and
  (4) have staff return with a report at the next meeting regarding the $1 ownership at the end
  of the lease of the equipment and what the additional monthly payment would be. (*See item
  32 for additional information on the equipment lease).

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

28. District 5 Regional Bikeways - Mission Viejo railroad N/S Corridor Trail and the
  Jeronimo/Chrisanta Trail

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Mayor Goodell, to (1) adopt
  Resolution 20-53 to Amend the Fiscal Year 2020-2021 Budget to Account for the $220,000
  Award to the City, Which Will be Expended on the District 5 Regional Bikeways - Mission
  Viejo railroad N/S Corridor Trail and the Jeronimo/Chrisanta Trail; (2) create capital
  improvement program (CIP) project 327 to receive grant funds from the Orange County
  Transportation Authority (OCTA) for environmental and engineering services for the District
  5 Regional Bikeways - Mission Viejo railroad N/S Corridor Trail and the Jeronimo/Chrisanta
  Trail; and (3) approve contract and authorize City staff to issue a purchase order to Carlson
City Council Minutes  7  October 13, 2020
   Strategic Land Solutions, Inc. (CSLS) (A20-31) in an amount not to exceed $42,360.00 using
  Bicycle Corridor Improvement Program Grant funds.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

29. Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Received report from Council Member Bucknum.

30. Transportation Corridor Agency (TCA) Report

  Received report from Mayor Pro Tem Kelley.

  Council Member Bucknum asked for a report to the City Council concerning an inquiry to
  request the Grand Jury look into the conduct of the City of San Clemente in regards to the
  public funds they are using to conduct smear campaigns against individual council members
  in different cities.

  City Attorney Bill Curley stated that it can be agendized for City Council discussion and
  direction.

STAFF REPORTS

19. COVID-19 UPDATE

  Emergency Operations Manager Paul Catsimanes presented the staff report.

  The Council received and filed the report.

32. CalPERS Pension Plan Actuarial Valuation Report for June 30, 2019

  *Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas clarified information on item 27 in regards
  to the equipment lease purchase for the Oso Creek Golf Course. She stated that there is a
  clause at the end of that lease document, under section 1101, for a $1 equipment buyout.

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Council Member Sachs asked staff to prepare a report for a future Council Meeting that
  establishes an 80% baseline trigger if the evaluation report, including the 115 Trust, falls
  below 80% to require action by the City Council and a staff recommendation to get the City
  back up to 80%.

  The City Council received and filed the report.
City Council Minutes  8  October 13, 2020
 33. Authorization to File an Appeal of SCAG’s Draft Regional Housing Needs Assessment
  Allocation of 2,211 Housing Units to the City of Mission Viejo

  The following expressed opposition to the appeal: Cesar Covarrubias, The Kennedy
  Commission; Marilyn Schroeder, M.V.; and Rona Henry.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, direct staff to
  prepare an appeal of the 2,211 housing units allocated to the City of Mission Viejo as part of
  the state-mandated Regional Housing Needs Assessment.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

34. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum announced that she attended ribbon cutting events at Christopher Park
and at Craycraft Park for the opening of the public restroom. She thanked the Boy Scouts that
assisted with the restroom project at Craycraft Park and complimented Director of Public Services
Keith Rattay for his selection of the monument of the young girl softball player that was installed
at the park. Council Member Bucknum announced that she took golf lessons over the summer and
participated in the golf tournament at Camp Pendleton and she will also be playing in the
tournament at Oso Creek Golf Course for the Orange County Youth Sports Foundation. She
thanked staff for their work during this COVID-19 Pandemic and encouraged residents to buy local
during the upcoming holiday season. Lastly, Council Member Bucknum reminded residents to vote
and stated that the less people that touch a ballot, the better.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths said that he enjoyed the golf tournament at Camp Pendleton and he
recommended that voters either walk their ballot in or vote in person.

Council Member Sachs

35. Update of Temporary Sign Policy Regulation

  Council Member Sachs presented his report.

City Council Minutes  9  October 13, 2020
   Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to (1)
  consolidate all the functions of the temporary sign policy to the Community
  Development/Code Enforcement Department for a unified system; (2) include notice to
  homeowner associations and commercial properties in the policy; and(3) enhance the policy
  map to show the actual right-of-way areas.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

Council Member Sachs announced that there will be additional Community Development Block
Grant Funds (CDBG) available for businesses and COVID relief that will be discussed at a future
Council Meeting, along with the qualifications that are necessary to obtain these grants. He asked
Chief Vuong to prepare a report for the next Council Meeting to provide an update on the School
Resource Officers (SRO’s) since school is back in session. Lastly, Council Member Sachs discussed
a former Council Member's repeated public comment accusations against the Council that are not
fact-based, and he outlined some questionable incidents that occurred in the past with this former
Council Member.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley outlined ribbon cutting ceremonies she attended and indicated that it was
wonderful to get back out in the community. She gave kudos to City Staff for the renovations at
Christopher Park and the installation of restrooms at Craycraft Park. She announced that she and
her husband volunteered at the golf tournament at Camp Pendleton and she thanked staff for their
great work. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley stated that this month’s character word is “respect” and next
month’s is “thankfulness.” She noted that the next blood drive will be held on Monday, November
16, 2020, in the Saddleback Room at City Hall. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley thanked Gayle Wood for
her volunteerism with the Marines at Camp Pendleton. She also noted that schools are open again
on a hybrid schedule and finally, she outlined voting options and reminded everyone to vote.

Mayor Goodell

Mayor Goodell stated that opening the parks and rededicating Christopher Park and Craycraft Park
were very special occasions and the first events the City has had since COVID. He thanked City
staff for taking advantage of the down time to make those parks wonderful and all the other projects
they have been working on. Mayor Goodell shared that he had a great time playing golf with his
fellow Council Members at Camp Pendleton and he thanked John Petki for organizing a group of
players that came down from Mission Viejo to participate in the tournament and support the
Marines. Mayor Goodell stated that he is hoping that the County will be moving to the Orange Tier
for COVID-19 reopening and he asked that residents still social distance, keep wearing masks, and
respect each other so more businesses can open. He also encouraged residents to get tested so they
know their health status.

City Council Minutes  10  October 13, 2020
 ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:45 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Goodell adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, October 27, 2020, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of November 10, 2020

City Council Minutes  11  October 13, 2020
